title: Barbarians at the Gate: AI-driven research for systems (ADRS)
summary: An LLM-driven generate-evaluate-refine loop built on OpenEvolve produced systems algorithms in case studies, with the abstract reporting up to 5.0x runtime improvements or 50% cost reductions over baselines. Solutions are checked with simulators or real systems, which is the validation basis. The results are on specific case studies rather than a general claim, and the work is a preprint.
ai_technology: OpenEvolve (LLM-driven evolutionary code search, ADRS framework)

evidence.tested: Generated systems algorithms were run against predefined workloads in real systems or simulators and compared with state-of-the-art human designs across case studies (cloud load balancing, MoE inference, LLM SQL queries, transaction scheduling). The abstract reports up to 5.0x runtime improvement or 50% cost reduction.
evidence.unknown: The method assumes a reliable verifier, which the authors present as a precondition; the page has no dedicated limitations section and the work is a preprint.
evidence.ai_role: An LLM-driven generate-evaluate-refine loop (penEvolve, an open-source ADRS instance) proposed the algorithms.
